title: ChatKit ASP.NET Core Browser Runtime Verification
verification_method: Execution and inspection of the node-based packaged runtime tests plus the maintained browser-host contract documentation.
preconditions: The packaged runtime dependencies under src/Incursa.OpenAI.ChatKit.AspNetCore/ClientApp/chatkit-runtime are restored.
The node-based runtime tests execute successfully.
scope: This verification slice covers direct proof for packaged browser-runtime option projection, browser callback resolution and payload validation, host control and event mirroring, multi-host mount behavior, and visible runtime failure rendering. It intentionally complements rather than replaces the render-time host and endpoint proof in VER-CHATKIT-ASPNETCORE-0001.
expected_result: The packaged runtime translates the serialized host config into supported ChatKitOptions, resolves callback registries and validates payloads with clear failures, preserves client-first widget action handling, mirrors the upstream control and event surface on the rendered host, mounts each host once, and renders visible runtime errors when mounting fails.
procedure: Run the node-based packaged runtime tests in src/Incursa.OpenAI.ChatKit.AspNetCore/ClientApp/chatkit-runtime.
Review the runtimeHost.js bridge and its helper modules against the current browser-runtime requirement set.
Confirm that the maintained README and tag-helper contract documentation match the mirrored host control and event surface.
status_summary: The packaged runtime now has direct executable proof for config translation, callback resolution, widget-action ordering, mirrored imperative host methods, mirrored chatkit.* events, and deferred custom-element definition handling. The main remaining gap is full browser end-to-end proof against the real upstream custom element in a live page; this verification slice still relies on the focused node harness rather than a browser automation layer.
